newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Opatovice power still a buy - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Czech Opatovice power still a buy - analyst.

text.p: Shares of Czech utility Elektrarny Opatovice (EOP) remain a "buy" even though its share price has surpassed four times the stock's nominal value, gaining more than 40 percent this year.

"In shares of Elektrarny Opatovice we see a good investment opportunity for investors with a medium and a long-term investment horizon," Blanka Houhova, an analyst with a Prague broker BH Securities said.
The eastern Czech utility uses high-efficiency combined heat and electrical production technology, helping it to post strong profit results, analysts said.

The company shows one of the highest rates of earnings growth in the sector. As total turnover has remained at around 2.3 billion crowns for the past three years, while nine-month 1996 total revenue was up 16 percent to 1.84 billion crowns.

Analysts gave a range of forecasts for 1996 net profit to rise to between 550 million crowns to 620 million crowns, up from 1995's net of 535 million crowns, a five percent increase over the previous calendar year.

"Last year's results were positively influenced by the early start of winter, and also its length will have a positive impact on this year results. The same is true about the early start of this year's heating season," Houhova said.
The company paid out almost 40 percent of its 1995 profit with a gross dividend of 180 crowns per share, up from 160 crowns on 1994 profit.

Some analysts worry however that Opatovice's 1996 share buying spree might cut into dividends, as it finances its newly acquired stakes in Prague heating utility Prazska Teplarenska and power utility Vychodoceska Energetika.
"The height of dividends remains a question, as the management considers ways how to finance this year's huge acquisitions," Michal Klusak of AKRO Capital said.

Elektrarny Opatovice's ownership structure has remained fairly stable. As of the beginning of December, the largest shareholders were the SPIF Cesky fund with 19 percent, fund IPF Komercni Banky with 14 percent, and the bank, Komercni Banka with 10 percent.
Shares of Elektrarny Opatovice traded on the Prague Stock Exchange on Monday at 4,371 crowns, 11 crowns lower than Friday's close.
